manage.accounts.title: Accounts
manage.accounts.description: Log in to each store whose games you want in your library. You can be logged in to several stores, and to several accounts of one store, at once.
manage.accounts.expired_hint: {store} no longer accepts your saved login. Log in again to refresh your library and to install, update or play online games.
manage.accounts.offline: You’re offline. Logging in and refreshing need an internet connection.
manage.accounts.login_hint: Log in to see your {store} games in the library.
manage.accounts.logout_confirm.title: Log out of {store}?
manage.accounts.logout_confirm.descripti: Installed games stay on disk. To install, update or launch online games from this store you need to log in again.
manage.accounts.account_expired: Log in again to use this account
manage.accounts.signed_out_installed_one: Logged out · 1 game installed with it
manage.accounts.signed_out_installed_oth: Logged out · {count} games installed with it
manage.accounts.logout_account_confirm.i: The game installed with this account stays on disk. To update or launch it, log in to this account again.
The {count} games installed with this account stay on disk. To update or launch them, log in to this account again.
manage.accounts.optional_login_hint: Log in to {store} to add every game you own and the games your family shares.
manage.accounts.optional_logout_descript: Installed {store} games stay in your library. Games you haven’t installed leave it until you log in again.
manage.stores.title: Stores
manage.stores.description: Store pages open in your browser. Games you buy appear in the library after a refresh.
manage.stores.blurb.epic: Weekly free games and the Epic catalogue.
manage.stores.blurb.itch: Indie games, game jams and pay-what-you-want releases.
manage.stores.login_hint: Purchases appear after you log in.
manage.deals.title: Deals
manage.deals.info: Deals open in your browser. GreenManGaming and Humble sell keys for other launchers, such as Steam.
manage.deals.unavailable: Couldn’t load deals. Check your connection and try again.
manage.deals.library_only: Only games related to my library
manage.deals.source.key: {store} · key for another store or launcher
manage.downloads.title: Downloads
manage.downloads.current.paused_queue: Downloads are paused. Resume to start the next item.
manage.downloads.current.paused: Paused. The download continues from where it stopped when you resume.
manage.downloads.queue.title: Up next · {count}
manage.downloads.stop_install.title: Stop installing “{title}”?
manage.downloads.stop_install.descriptio: Keeping the downloaded files lets a later install continue where it stopped.
manage.downloads.stop_update.title: Stop updating “{title}”?
manage.downloads.stop_update.description: The installed version stays playable. You can update later.
manage.downloads.history.title: History
manage.downloads.empty.title: No downloads
manage.downloads.empty.description: Games you install or update appear here, with their progress and history.
manage.login.title: Log in to {store}
manage.login.another_in_browser: If the page signs you in to an account that’s already here, log out on the {store} website first, then sign in with the other account.
manage.login.input_placeholder: Paste the code or address here
manage.login.step.sign_in: Sign in on the store’s website
manage.login.step.opened: The sign-in page opened in your browser.
manage.login.auto_detect: Irori signs in as soon as you copy it.
manage.login.window.waiting: Sign in in the window that opened. Irori finishes as soon as {store} confirms it.
manage.login.window.missing: Irori's sign-in window isn't installed, so the page opened in your browser.
manage.login.window.failed: The sign-in window couldn't open, so the page opened in your browser.
manage.steam.qr_hint: In the Steam Mobile app, open Steam Guard and scan this code.
manage.steam.password_note: Your password goes to Steam only. Irori doesn’t keep it.
manage.steam.approve_on_phone: Approve the login in the Steam Mobile app.
manage.steam.device_code: Enter the Steam Guard code from the Steam Mobile app.
manage.steam.email_code: Enter the code Steam sent to your email at {domain}.
manage.steam.email_code_plain: Enter the code Steam sent to your email.
manage.steam.email_confirm: Open the link in the email Steam sent you.
manage.steam.error.password: Steam didn’t accept that account name or password.
manage.steam.error.code: That code didn’t work. Check it and try again.
manage.steam.error.rate_limited: Steam is limiting logins from this computer. Wait a few minutes, then try again.
manage.wine.title: Wine manager
manage.wine.description_macos: Download Wine builds for Windows games, or use an installed CrossOver or Whisky runtime.
manage.wine.description: Download Proton and Wine builds for Windows games, and see every build on this system.
manage.wine.description_running_one: Download Proton and Wine builds for Windows games. 1 install running.
manage.wine.description_running_other: Download Proton and Wine builds for Windows games. {count} installs running.
manage.wine.source.ge_proton: Proton with extra game fixes by GloriousEggroll, meant to run through umu outside of Steam. A good default for most games.
manage.wine.source.proton_cachyos: Proton from CachyOS with performance patches and extra tools such as DXVK-Sarek and D7VK.
manage.wine.source.wine_ge: Wine with Proton’s game fixes, for running without the Steam runtime. No longer updated upstream.
manage.wine.source.wine_kron4ek: Plain, staging and TkG Wine builds by Kron4ek.
manage.wine.fetch_failed: Couldn’t fetch releases: {error}. GitHub may be limiting requests; try again later.
manage.wine.remove_confirm.title: Remove {version}?
manage.wine.remove_confirm.default_descr: This is the default Wine for all games. Games without their own Wine setting will need another build before they can start.
manage.wine.remove_confirm.description: Games set to use this build will need another Wine or Proton build. You can download it again at any time.
manage.wine.empty.title: No versions found
manage.wine.empty.description: Refresh to fetch the release list again.
manage.wine.system.empty.title: No Wine or Proton found
manage.wine.system.empty.description: Install a build from one of the other tabs, or add a folder that contains one.
manage.wine.custom.title: Custom paths
manage.wine.custom.hint: Add folders with Wine or Proton builds that Irori doesn’t find on its own.
manage.wine.custom.prompt: Choose a Wine or Proton folder
manage.onboarding.welcome.title: Welcome to Irori
manage.onboarding.welcome.description: Irori brings your Epic, GOG, Amazon and ZOOM games into one library and runs Windows games with Wine and Proton. A few steps set it up.
manage.onboarding.import.title: Bring over your Heroic setup
manage.onboarding.import.description: Irori found Heroic Games Launcher. Importing keeps your store logins, installed games, per-game settings, favourites and categories. Heroic itself is left unchanged.
manage.onboarding.stores.title: Connect your stores
manage.onboarding.stores.description: Log in to the stores you buy games from. You can skip this and log in later from Accounts.
manage.onboarding.stores.offline: You’re offline. Logging in needs an internet connection.
manage.onboarding.folder.title: Where should games go?
manage.onboarding.folder.description: New installs go into this folder. You can pick another folder for each install, and change this later in Settings.
manage.onboarding.folder.prompt: Choose the folder for new installs
manage.onboarding.done.title: You’re all set
manage.onboarding.done.no_stores: You can log in to stores from Accounts at any time, and add other games from the library.
manage.onboarding.done.stores: Logged in to {stores}. Your games appear in the library as each store finishes loading.
manage.downloads.files.title: Files
manage.accounts.hidden_detail: Its games are left out of your library. The sign-in and installed games are kept.
manage.accounts.local_hint: Read from {store} on this computer, no login needed. Install and update games in {store}.
manage.accounts.local_missing: {store} wasn’t found on this computer. If it’s installed somewhere else, set its folder in Settings.
manage.accounts.local_hidden_detail: Its games are left out of your library.
manage.emulators.title: Emulators
manage.emulators.description: Emulators play games made for consoles and older computers. Install one for each system you want to play; Irori sets it up for you.
manage.emulators.not_downloadable: Irori can’t download {engine} for this computer. Install it from Flathub or your distribution’s software centre and Irori finds it, or choose its program below.
manage.emulators.no_build: {engine} has no version for this computer yet. It runs on {hosts}.
manage.emulators.use_program: Use a program on this computer…
manage.emulators.remove_message: Its files are deleted. Games set to use this version will ask you to choose another one.
manage.emulators.cores.title: Cores · {installed} of {total} installed
manage.emulators.cores.description: RetroArch plays each system with a core. Irori installs the recommended core when you first play a game; you can install others here.
manage.emulators.systems.description: Each system plays with its default emulator unless you choose another one for a game.
manage.emulators.configure.title: {engine} settings
manage.emulators.configure.description: These apply to every game you play with {engine}. You can change them for one game in that game’s settings.
manage.emulators.configure.own_settings_: Irori leaves {engine}’s configuration alone and only tells it where your BIOS files are. Turn this on if you set {engine} up yourself.
manage.engines.option.fullscreen.label: Full screen
manage.engines.option.vsync.label: Vertical sync
manage.engines.option.vsync.help: Matches the frame rate to your display to stop tearing. Turn it off only if games feel slow to respond.
manage.engines.option.show_fps.label: Show frame rate
manage.engines.option.show_fps.help: Shows frames per second in a corner of the screen.
manage.engines.option.video_driver.label: Graphics driver
manage.engines.option.video_driver.help: How the game is drawn. Leave it on Automatic; if a game shows a black screen or crashes at start, try OpenGL.
manage.engines.option.pause_in_backgroun: Pauses the game while you use another window.
manage.engines.option.aspect_ratio.label: Keep the original shape
manage.engines.option.aspect_ratio.help: Shows games in the shape they were made for instead of stretching them to the window.
manage.engines.option.exit_on_quit.label: Close DOSBox when the game quits
manage.engines.option.exit_on_quit.help: Closes DOSBox when the game’s program ends, instead of leaving you at the DOS prompt.
manage.emulators.folders.title: Game folders
manage.emulators.folders.description: Irori finds console and retro games in these folders, sorts them by system and adds new ones as they appear.
manage.emulators.bios.title: BIOS files
manage.emulators.bios.description: Some systems need a startup file from your own console, called a BIOS. Irori never downloads them; point it at the folder where you keep yours.
manage.emulators.bios.missing: Needs a BIOS from your console: {files}
manage.emulators.bios.unrecognized: BIOS found but not recognised, it may not work: {files}
manage.setup.title: Set up emulation
manage.setup.folders.intro: Where are your games? Choose the folders that hold your console and retro games; subfolders are included and Irori works out the system of each game.
manage.setup.emulators.intro: Irori recommends one emulator for each system it found. Install them in one go; you can change them later on the Emulators page.
manage.setup.done.title: You’re all set
manage.setup.done.games: {count} games are in your library, ready to play.
manage.setup.done.no_games: Add a folder with games on the Emulators page whenever you’re ready.
manage.onboarding.lutris.title: Coming from Lutris?
manage.onboarding.lutris.description: Irori can bring over your Lutris games (Windows, Linux and emulated), favourites, categories and playtime. Lutris stays as it is.
manage.launchers.title: Other launchers
manage.launchers.description: Battle.net, the EA app, Ubisoft Connect and the Rockstar Games Launcher keep their own accounts. Irori sets each one up in its own Wine prefix with the official installer; you sign in and install games in the launcher, and they appear in your library. Irori never sees your login.
manage.launchers.description_windows: Show the games you installed with Battle.net, the EA app, Ubisoft Connect or the Rockstar Games Launcher in your library. They start through their launcher.
manage.launchers.anticheat: Many online games from these launchers use anti-cheat that refuses to run under Wine. Look a game up on its compatibility tab or ProtonDB before you buy it.
manage.launchers.about.battlenet: Blizzard and Activision games: World of Warcraft, Diablo, Overwatch, Call of Duty.
manage.launchers.about.ea: EA games, including those you own on Steam or Epic that need the EA app.
manage.launchers.about.ubisoft: Ubisoft games, including those that need Ubisoft Connect to start.
manage.launchers.about.rockstar: Grand Theft Auto, Red Dead Redemption and other Rockstar games.
